statement_record.book: For F : C ⇄ D : G, an adjunction F ⊣ G is equivalently encoded by any of six data: (i) a natural family of isos D(Fc,d) ≅ C(c,Gd); (ii) η and ε satisfying the triangle identities; (iii) η alone such that f♯ ↦ Gf♯ ∘ η_c is an iso D(Fc,d) ≅ C(c,Gd); (iv) ε alone such that g♭ ↦ ε_d ∘ Fg♭ is an iso; (v) η whose component at each c is an INITIAL object of c ↓ G; (vi) ε whose component at each d is a TERMINAL object of F ↓ d.
statement_record.intree: (i) is `Class Adjunction` (Theory/Adjunction.v:130, hom-setoid form) and `Class Adjunction_Hom` (Adjunction/Hom.v:72, natural iso of hom-bifunctors in [D^op ∏ C, Sets]); (ii) is `Class Adjunction_Transform`; (i)⟺(ii) is proved in both directions and in both packagings (Adjunction_from_Transform / Adjunction_to_Transform, and Adjunction_Hom_to_Transform / Adjunction_Transform_to_Hom, Adjunction_Hom_to_Universal / Adjunction_Universal_to_Hom). Displays (4.2.8)/(4.2.9) are to_adj_unit / from_adj_counit; the ∃!-form of (v)/(vi) is adj_univ + to_adj_unit and adj_univ_impl. `UniversalArrow c U := Initial (=(c) ↓ U)` with AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows gives (v) ⇒ adjunction.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the (i)⟺(ii) leg of the six-way equivalence is closed in both directions. The remaining clauses appear as one-directional fragments (see gap).

gap: Three of the six legs are one-directional, and the theorem is nowhere stated as a single equivalence. (a) Clauses (iii)/(iv) exist only in the forward direction: given F ⊣ U, to_adj_unit / from_adj_counit identify the transposition maps and `adj` supplies invertibility; there is NO in-tree lemma taking a bare natural η : Id ⟹ U ◯ F (with F and U BOTH GIVEN) whose composite fmap[U](−) ∘ η is bijective and producing F ⊣ U — the only route, Build_Adjunction' via universal arrows, CONSTRUCTS its own left adjoint (LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows) instead of accepting the given F. (b) Clause (v) holds only in the direction (v) ⇒ adjunction (AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows); no in-tree lemma converts a given F ⊣ U into `UniversalArrow c U` witnesses, i.e. no proof that η_c is an INITIAL object of the comma category =(c) ↓ U — the universal property survives only in the ∃!-form (adj_univ / to_adj_unit), unpackaged from the comma category. (c) Clause (vi) has no comma-category form at all in either direction: `adj_univ_impl` gives the ∃!-property of ε_d, but there is no dual of UniversalArrow/AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows (grep for RightAdjointFunctor|CoUniversal|TerminalArrow → 0 hits), so 'ε_d is terminal in F ↓ d' is never stated and no adjunction is ever built from a counit alone.

statement_record.book: Any adjoint pair F : C ⇄ D : G restricts to an equivalence between the full subcategory of C spanned by the c with η_c invertible and the full subcategory of D spanned by the d with ε_d invertible.
statement_record.intree: AdjointEquivalence_to_Equivalence : an adjunction all of whose unit AND counit components are invertible is an equivalence of categories; MLocal_Subcategory : the full subcategory spanned by the objects at which the unit of a (idempotent) monad is invertible, shown reflective (Idempotent_Reflective, line 345) and equivalent to the Eilenberg–Moore category (Idempotent_EM_Equivalence, line 464).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the DEGENERATE case is proved — the equivalence is obtained when the fixed subcategories are the whole of C and D (every η_c and ε_d invertible). The restriction of a general adjunction to its two fixed full subcategories is not constructed.

gap: Nothing in the tree forms the two fixed full subcategories OF A GENERAL ADJUNCTION and restricts the adjunction to them.
